question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Teja is a successful businessman; he always __makes hay when the moon shines__.

options.text: makes hay while the sun sets
makes hay while the sun shines
makes hey while the moon rises
makes hay while the stars twinkle

solution:
The correct answer is: "**makes hay while the sun shines**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original phrase "**he always makes hay when the moon shines**" is a play on the traditional idiom "**make hay while the sun shines**."
 
• The original idiom means to take advantage of favourable conditions or opportunities. (अनुकूल परिस्थितियों या अवसरों का लाभ उठाना)
 
 
• **Example**: *Recognizing the potential for growth, Alex decided to make hay while the sun shines__ and invested in the booming tech industry.*
 
 
 
• In the context of Teja being a successful businessman, it suggests that he seizes opportunities when they arise.
 
• The suggested substitution, "**he always makes hay when the sun shines**," adheres more closely to the conventional idiom.
 
• The phrase "**when the sun shines**" reinforces the idea of utilizing favourable conditions for one's benefit.

Thus, **option 2** is the correct answer.
